1. (Currently Amended) An alarm system comprising: a physiological monitor capable of triggering a first alarm in response to an alarm condition; and a station located remotely from the physiological monitor, wherein the station is capable of receiving an input from the physiological monitor and triggering a second alarm in response to the alarm condition, and wherein when the second alarm is not acknowledged __within a predetermined time period__, the station is capable of sending an output to the physiological monitor to initiate an escalated alarm at the physiological monitor __that is different from the first alarm__.

2. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the second alarm is capable of being acknowledged by an operator input before expiration of a timer.

3. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm comprises an inaudible alarm.

4. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm.

5. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm comprises an audible alarm and the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm that is louder than the first alarm.

6. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the first alarm and the second alarm are triggered substantially simultaneously.

7. (Original) The system of claim 1, wherein the station located remotely from the physiological monitor is part of a central patient management system.

8. (Previously presented) A physiological monitor comprising: a processor programmed to: trigger a first alarm in response to an alarm condition; send an output to a remotely located station, wherein the output triggers a second alarm in response to the alarm condition; and receive an input from the remotely located station, wherein the input causes physiological monitor to initiate an escalated alarm.

9. (Previously presented) The physiological monitor of claim 8, wherein the processor is programmed to send an output to a wireless device when the escalated alarm is not acknowledged.

10. (Previously presented) The physiological monitor of claim 8, wherein the first alarm comprises an inaudible alarm.

11. (Previously presented) The physiological monitor of claim 8, wherein the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm.

12. (Previously presented) The physiological monitor of claim 8, wherein the first alarm comprises an audible alarm and the escalated alarm comprises an audible alarm that is louder than the first alarm.

13. (Previously presented) The physiological monitor of claim 8, wherein the first alarm and the second alarm are triggered substantially simultaneously.

14. (Previously presented) A method, comprising: triggering a first alarm in response to an alarm condition; triggering a second alarm remote from the first location in response to the alarm condition; and escalating the first alarm if neither of the first or second alarms are acknowledged with a certain time.

15. (Previously presented) The method of claim 14, wherein triggering the first alarm comprises triggering an inaudible alarm.

16. (Currently Amended) A system comprising: a processor programmed to trigger an alarm in response to an alarm condition; a memory capable of storing alarm data associated with the alarm, wherein the alarm data comprises an alarm type and a time that the alarm was triggered __and an escalation status indicating whether the alarm has been escalated__; and a display capable of displaying the alarm data.

17. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 16, wherein the system is part of a physiological monitor or a central management system.

18. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 16, wherein the alarm data comprises information about a level of escalation of the alarm.

19. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 16, wherein the alarm data comprises information about an acknowledgement of the alarm.

20. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 16, wherein the processor is programmed to send the alarm data to one or more wireless devices.
